newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Refining Co shuts crude unit Mar 4-21.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Refining Co shuts crude unit Mar 4-21.

text.p: Singapore Refining Co (SRC) will shut down its 90,000-barrel-per-day crude distillation unit (CDU) for scheduled maintenance during March 4-21, a company spokesman said on Monday,
Traders said the crude unit's turnaround had already commenced on Sunday.

They also said during the maintenance, associated secondary units were being closed, including a 14,000-bpd vacuum distillation unit (VDU), an 18,000-bpd hydrocracker, and an 18-million-cubic-feet-per-day hydrogen plant.
A 32,000-bpd visbreaker would also be shut down "within the next few days for 10 days", a company source said.
Company sources told Reuters the turnaround would not prompt any serious shortage in products as the two other CDUs would still be running.

SRC's 285,000-bpd refinery at Pulau Merlimau off southwestern Singapore is co-owned by the Singapore Petroleum Corp (SPC), British Petroleum and Caltex, a joint-venture of U.S. majors Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
The spokesman also said the 14,000-bpd hydrocracker No.2 which shut down February 18 was restarted February 23.
